concept.title: Term List (Definition List)
concept.abstract: This section covers Term Lists (Definition Lists) in HTML — structures that associate a term with its corresponding definition or description, emphasizing term-description relationships rather than value comparison across columns — and two scenarios: a native HTML <dl> element with <dt> and <dd> pairs, and a <ul> list following the bold-label pattern where each <li> begins with a <strong> term followed by a separator and definition text. The converter maps each term list to <dl><dlentry><dt><dd> in concept and reference topics, or nests it inside <step><info> as supporting information in task topics, based on the heading classification and content context.

conbody.p: A term list, also known as a definition list, is an HTML structure used to associate terms with their corresponding definitions or descriptions. It is commonly used to present technical terminology, configuration options, error codes, connection modes, and other reference information, with each term followed by one or more explanatory statements. Unlike a table, a definition list emphasizes the relationship between a term and its description rather than comparing values across multiple columns.

Term lists improve readability by allowing related definitions to be scanned without interrupting the flow of the surrounding content. Publishing systems, accessibility technologies, and content management systems rely on correctly structured definition lists to preserve the relationship between each term and its description across different output formats.

In well-structured HTML, term lists are authored either as native <dl> elements containing <dt> and <dd> pairs or as unordered lists where each <li> begins with a <strong> term followed by a separator and its corresponding definition. The native <dl> structure provides the clearest semantic representation, while the bold-label pattern offers an alternative that the converter can also recognize.

The converter detects both supported HTML patterns when generating DITA output. Native <dl> elements map directly to DITA <dl>, while recognized <ul> lists that follow the bold-label pattern are converted to the same DITA definition list structure. Each term becomes a DITA <dt>, each definition becomes a <dd>, and related pairs are grouped within a <dlentry>.
conbody.note: Use native HTML <dl>, <dt>, and <dd> elements wherever possible to represent term-definition relationships. Although the converter recognizes supported <ul> patterns, native definition lists provide the clearest semantic structure and produce the most reliable conversion results.
conbody.p: The following table summarizes the DITA elements used to represent term lists during HTML-to-DITA conversion:

row.entry: Groups a single term–definition pair. Contains exactly one <dt> and one or more <dd> elements.
Definition term. Maps from the <dt> element or the <strong> run at the start of a <li> item.
Definition description. Maps from the <dd> element or the non-bold text that follows the term in the same <li> item.

conbody.p: Definition lists are commonly used inside concept and reference topics. When a definition list appears in a task topic, it is typically placed inside <step><info> as supporting information.
